title: Non-Rock Alternatives to Shoreline Protection Demonstration (LA-0016)
intro: A three-stop look at this CPRA project: where it is, what it changes, and its status and funding.

steps.title: Where it's at
steps.body: This project is along the eastern shoreline of Vermilion Bay, on Shark Island in Iberia Parish.

media.alt: Aerial view of Shark Island's shoreline on Vermilion Bay, Iberia Parish (2024 aerial imagery).

steps.title: What it is changing
steps.body: Rock is the usual way to armor an eroding shoreline, but it does not work everywhere — some sites have soil too soft, or are too hard to reach, for standard rock revetments. This project tested several non-rock alternatives to protect the shoreline from erosion, with the results used to guide future coastal restoration choices statewide.

steps.title: Timeline / Completion Date
steps.body: Project Status: Completed. Estimated Cost: $7,358,699 ($916,305 in state dollars). Funding Source: Coastal Wetlands Planning, Protection and Restoration Act (CWPPRA).
